claim: A grantee who does not see the house's money sees their own grant's limit on the phone's Today screen, and no one else's (ADR 0253; the founder, 2026-10-01: 'Show their own limit (Recommended)', then, on how: 'Record the grantee (Recommended)'; rejected: 'Look it up each load', 'Leave it'). The grants register's one notification writer, tell() in organizations/authority-grants.service.ts, records the grantee as metadata.granteeUserId, taken from the grant, on every authority_grant_* notice, and keeps sending issued and re-approved notices to every owner and the grantee. In GET /mobile/feed a card built from a notification gets its message as the subtitle for a caller who does not see money also when isOwnGrantNotice(type, meta, userId) holds: the type is authority_grant_issued or authority_grant_reapproved (OWN_LIMIT_NOTIFICATION_TYPES, exactly those two, neither on MONEY_FREE_NOTIFICATION_TYPES), the metadata is an object whose granteeUserId is a non-empty string, and it equals userId, getFeed's first parameter, never reassigned or shadowed, which the controller fills from the token's user.userId. A row written before the grantee was recorded, an owner's copy of someone else's grant read after a demotion, a grantee given as anything but a non-empty string, and a caller with no id all keep the neutral line; the card's meta stays cut by nonMoneyMeta to NON_MONEY_META_KEYS, which does not name granteeUserId, and the gate is the service's only reader of that key, so granteeUserId never reaches such a caller. Owner and manager output is unchanged. Behaviour: mobile/mobile-feed-money-for-staff.spec.ts (the grant writer's notice pinned to the spec's fixtures). This verify fails on ebd69b364 and 7fdf4f95f and kills 33 of 33 source mutations, among them the writer dropping the grantee or recording the actor, the gate returning true, ignoring the type, accepting an empty or non-string grantee or comparing to the house id, getFeed's userId reassigned or shadowed, and granteeUserId named on NON_MONEY_META_KEYS (either quote), added to it later, kept by the cut or spread onto a card.
